context: seasonal process plant · mills, boilers and turbines; must be ready for the crushing season

brief.intro: New to this project type? A sugar factory squeezes juice out of cane (or extracts it from beet), cleans it, boils off the water in a chain of evaporators, grows sugar crystals in vacuum pans, spins them out in centrifuges and dries them. A cane factory also runs its own power station: the leftover fibre (bagasse) is burned in high-pressure boilers that drive turbine-generators, and the exhaust steam does the evaporation. So it is a process plant and a power plant together, full of large vessels, pipework and rotating machinery, much of it outdoors or in open steel structures. And it is seasonal — the cane is harvested in a fixed campaign each year. Miss the start of the season and the plant earns nothing until the next one, so the start date is as hard as any contract date.

scope.name: Site preparation & enabling
scope.desc: Grading, access roads, temporary facilities and underground services.

scope.name: Building & machine foundations
scope.desc: Column footings plus the heavy bases, pits and trenches the machines sit on — set out from the equipment drawings.

scope.name: Steel structure & envelope
scope.desc: Portal frames, crane beams, roof and wall cladding, making the hall weather-tight.

scope.name: Industrial floor
scope.desc: Flat, hard-wearing floor slab, cast after the roof is on and before the machines move in.

scope.name: Cane yard & preparation
scope.desc: Weighbridge, cane tables, knives and shredder (beet: washing and slicing).

scope.name: Milling tandem / diffuser
scope.desc: Mills with turbine or electric drives that extract the juice.

scope.name: Centrifugals, drying & bagging
scope.desc: Centrifuges, dryer, grader, silo and bagging.

scope.name: Boilers & power house
scope.desc: Bagasse-fired boilers, turbine-generators and steam distribution.

scope.name: Plant utilities
scope.desc: Steam & condensate, Cooling water (spray pond / towers), Compressed air, Effluent treatment — the services every machine needs before it can run.

scope.name: Power supply & control
scope.desc: Substation, transformers, switchgear, cabling and the plant control system.

scope.name: Fire protection, HVAC & dust / fume extraction
scope.desc: Life-safety and environmental systems required for the operating permit.

scope.name: Commissioning & ramp-up
scope.desc: Water trials, steam trials, then first crush at the start of the season and stabilisation over the first weeks.

must_get_right: Work backwards from the first day of the crushing season — it is the one date that cannot move.
Boilers and turbine-generators are the longest-lead and longest-erection items; the process house cannot be steam-tested without them.
Heavy vessels are lifted into open structures in a set order; steelwork, vessel delivery and crane availability must be planned together.
Water and steam trials need weeks before first crush; do not let them be squeezed by late erection.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by plant area along the process line and by discipline, with every long-lead machine tracked from order to factory test, shipping and arrival.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar with the rainy season marked; the crushing-season start is a fixed constraint. Erection commonly runs extended shifts in the months before it.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Foundations → structures → vessels and mills erected in lift sequence → piping → insulation → electrics. Boilers and turbines run as a parallel long chain to steam blowing. Then water trials → steam trials → first crush at the season start. The critical path runs through the boilers or the mill tandem.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The process technology and vendor are fixed before design starts; vendor drawings for foundations arrive on the agreed dates; permanent power and water are available before cold commissioning; raw material for trial production is on site.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy machines need crane access and often must enter before the cladding or a wall is closed. Vendor supervisors are booked for fixed periods. Clean, dry, powered conditions are required before precision equipment is unpacked.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: late boilers or turbines, heavy-lift sequence clashes, piping volume underestimated, late grid interconnection, and trials squeezed before the season. Contingency is held before the season start.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by plant area and discipline; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the installation crews and the vendor supervisors — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
